text:
Maya Chen: customer escalated — says their dataset was decrypted around 2026-12-04 14:12-14:20 UTC. They provided a few request IDs but no mapping to our internal audit IDs. can we reconstruct? @Samir? :eyes:
Samir Patel: on it. first step: gather KMS audit logs + our audit_events for that window. suspect we need to correlate by request_id and principal/session id. do we have those fields in the current audit schema?
Eli Rosen: quick check — our audit_events currently include: event_type, actor_id, resource_id, request_id, timestamp, ip, path. KMS logs have kms_request_id, key_id, caller_identity, operation, response_status, and kms_timestamp. we don't currently surface kms_request_id into customer-facing events.
Jordan Lee: so mapping looks like: audit_events.request_id <> kms.kms_request_id. we sometimes capture gateway_request_id in headers (x-request-id). need to see if customer-supplied ids match x-request-id preserved in our KMS calls.
Maya Chen: customer gave these IDs: rq_8f3a1, rq_8f3a2, and an S3 object path. they say object was previewed by an internal user. they want a timeline for who called decrypt and when.
Samir Patel: start by pulling raw KMS logs for the key and timeframe.
Samir Patel: infra-sre — can you export raw KMS audit logs for key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-1234 for 2026-12-04T14:00:00Z -> 2026-12-04T14:30:00Z? include full request/response payloads.
infra-sre: copying the request. will run an export and put gz to s3: s3://redwood-internal/forensic/1812349999/kms/ — ETA 20m. :thumbsup:
Eli Rosen: while that's running, we should try correlate using SQL on audit_events:
Eli Rosen: ```sql
SELECT event_id, request_id, actor_id, resource_id, timestamp
FROM audit_events
WHERE timestamp >= '2026-12-04T14:00:00Z' AND timestamp <= '2026-12-04T14:30:00Z' AND resource_id LIKE '%s3://customer-bucket/%';
```
Eli Rosen: also check logs for gateway x-request-id -> search nginx/access logs and our proxy traces.
Jordan Lee: note: we discovered last month that our KMS client library sometimes drops x-request-id header when retries happen. there may be missing correlation for retried decrypt calls.
Maya Chen: that's concerning. if retries lost header, mapping could be incomplete. we need to call this out to customer as "ongoing investigation" but give them a timeline and what we can prove.
Samir Patel: agreed. short-term ask: preserve all raw logs (do not rotate) and snapshot the key policy history + CloudTrail entries. also lock key rotation until we finish. can SecOps hold rotation?
infra-sre: can hold rotation for 48h, adding retention hold + export. I will also create a read-only snapshot of CloudTrail bucket and tag it forensic:1812349999.
Maya Chen: good. next: schema gaps. we should propose adding these fields to audit_events so future investigations easier: kms_request_id, caller_principal_session, gateway_request_id, correlation_chain (list of ids). Also include raw_event_blob (redacted) for forensic purposes.
Samir Patel: +1. propose minimal event additions to ship ASAP: kms_request_id (string), gateway_request_id (string), principal_session_id (string). longer-term: canonical correlation_chain.
Eli Rosen: I can draft a small PR to the audit schema and producer to start emitting gateway_request_id from proxies and preserve x-request-id on retries. sample jq to extract candidate correlations from exported KMS gz: 
Eli Rosen: ```bash
zcat kms-export-20261204-*.gz | jq -r '. | select(.kms_timestamp >= "2026-12-04T14:00:00Z" and .kms_timestamp <= "2026-12-04T14:30:00Z") | [.kms_request_id, .key_id, .caller_identity.sessionId, .operation, .response_status] | @tsv'
```
Jordan Lee: FYI for customer-facing audit validation: we need to produce a timeline that maps our event_id and timestamps to their provided IDs and explain any gaps. also include a note about our retention and what we preserved.
Maya Chen: action items recap: 1) infra-sre export KMS logs and snapshot CloudTrail (ETA 20m) 2) Eli run SQL + correlation and share candidate timeline (ETA 1h) 3) Samir draft communication to customer legal/CS with current status (ETA 45m) 4) Sec propose schema change PR (Eli) and short-term mitigation to preserve x-request-id on retries.
Samir Patel: I'll start the customer message. propose we say: "We are preserving all relevant logs, have put key rotation on hold, and are reconstructing the timeline. We will share a preliminary timeline within 4 hours." keeps expectations.
Maya Chen: sounds good. keep thread updated. if anyone finds a direct match to their rq_8f3a1/2 call ids call it out in thread and cc me. :eyes:
audit-bot: forensic export job created: job_id=forensic-1812349999-1, status=running.
infra-sre: export complete and staged at s3://redwood-internal/forensic/1812349999/kms/kms-export-20261204-1400-1430.gz (checksum: sha256:5d9f..). also snapshot CloudTrail at s3://redwood-internal/forensic/1812349999/cloudtrail/
Eli Rosen: pulled export, running jq. earliest decrypt call in that range: kms_request_id=kms-rq-01aa, caller_session=svc-user-77, operation=Decrypt, kms_timestamp=2026-12-04T14:12:37Z, request_metadata includes x-request-id: rq_8f3a1 (yay).
Maya Chen: nice find. Samir please include that mapping to customer. this is what they needed.
Samir Patel: drafting now, will include the raw line and sanitized event id. ping if we need to redact anything for legal.
Jordan Lee: follow-up: we should log this procedure in postmortem-runbook note so CS can reuse for future escalations. small schema PR will be opened after we triage full window.
Maya Chen: thanks team. closing loop once customer acks.
